extracted.intended_audience: journalists, future journalists, and teachers of journalism; prospective seminar participants
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive page for the Poynter Institute outlining its mission, teaching approach, program types, faculty composition, and the specific learning outcomes participants should expect from seminars and courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep seminars small
rubrics_metrics.description: We keep seminars small, which means you get lots of individual attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes limited class size as a quality criterion to ensure individual attention for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on approach
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize a hands-on approach, so you participate in discussions, case studies, role-playing, and other exercises to get you involved in learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active learning methods (discussions, case studies, role-play, exercises) are core to instruction; passive lecture-only formats are disfavored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident and visiting faculty quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Our resident faculty includes distinguished professionals and scholars, all master teachers who bring special expertise to every session. Each seminar also includes visiting faculty, accomplished professionals who leave their jobs for a week to help teach, who spend time with you inside and outside the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion emphasizes instructors' professional distinction, teaching skill, and the inclusion of practicing professionals who provide real-world perspectives and extended availability to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence and nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: As a financially independent, nonprofit organization, the Institute is beholden to no interest except its own mission: to help journalists do their best work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is presented as a quality standard ensuring programs and instruction are guided by mission rather than external financial or commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of excellence and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: It promotes excellence and integrity in the practice of craft and in the practical leadership of successful businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institute evaluates success partly by how well it instills professional excellence and ethical integrity in journalism practice and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism that informs and enlightens public discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: It stands for a journalism that informs citizens and enlightens public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are framed around producing journalism with public service value; content and pedagogy are expected to support this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of independent journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: It carries forward Nelson Poynter's belief in the value of independent journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes independence as a qualitative standard shaping curriculum and institutional decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave better prepared to produce great journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: We want you to leave Poynter better prepared to produce great journalism, so that your readers, viewers, or listeners can make better-informed decisions and lead more satisfying lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall program effectiveness is measured by participants' increased preparedness to create impactful journalism that serves audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipped with new tools and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: We want you to be equipped with new tools and ideas to handle the challenges of producing quality news reports, programs, and publications, and with new ways of thinking about the work that you do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion focuses on acquisition of practical skills, tools, and conceptual approaches applicable to producing quality journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage to take risks and to do your best
rubrics_metrics.description: The courage to take risks and to do your best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an intended personal outcome — programs aim to foster participants' willingness to innovate and pursue ambitious journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher sense of self-esteem and power to shape your own career
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher sense of self-esteem and the power to shape your own career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to boost participants' professional confidence and agency in career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: New confidence in your craft
rubrics_metrics.description: New confidence in your craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction seeks to increase technical and professional confidence in journalistic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of the value of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognition of the value of diversity in the newsroom and in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity awareness and inclusion are explicit learning goals and measures of program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary to describe what you do and why
rubrics_metrics.description: The vocabulary to describe what you do and why, and what you stand for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs teach participants how to articulate their professional role, values, and rationale — an evaluative criterion for communication and professional identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire to continue your growth and share learning
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to continue your growth as a journalist and to share what you've learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term professional development and peer knowledge-sharing are intended outcomes used to judge program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: New network of supportive peers
rubrics_metrics.description: A new network of people who support you in your work, so your learning continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networking and ongoing peer support are explicit program benefits and criteria for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear picture of journalism's role in democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear picture of the special role of journalism in a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic understanding of journalism's democratic function is a stated learning objective and quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding that your life's work is valuable
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding that your life's work is valuable and that you can make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to instill purpose and meaning in participants' professional lives; this is presented as an important evaluative outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of program offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: In the years since its founding in 1975, the Institute has developed a rich mixture of teaching and research programs, ranging from sophisticated courses and seminars for professional journalists to basic classes at the elementary school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program breadth — from advanced professional seminars to elementary-level classes — is a feature and criterion for institutional scope and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of learning environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Seminar participants enjoy the variety of learning environments at the Institute: the intense discussion in the seminar rooms, the social interaction in the Great Hall, and the one-to-one conversation in the many small 'break-out' areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple learning settings (seminar rooms, social spaces, break-out areas) are part of the pedagogical design and quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of excellence drawn from founder
rubrics_metrics.description: In the development of all its programs, the Institute continues to draw on the standards of excellence set by Nelson Poynter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institute uses the founder's standards as an evaluative benchmark for curriculum, pedagogy, and institutional decisions.
